title: Reconstruct Itinerary
statement: You hold a pile of one-way plane tickets, each a pair [from, to]. The trip starts at JFK and must use every ticket exactly once. Return the order of airports visited. If more than one trip works, return the one that is smallest in alphabetical order. A valid trip always exists.

example.caption: From JFK, ATL is the smallest destination, but it is a dead end. The trip has to leave it for last.

idea.sentence: Walk forward taking the smallest ticket each time, but write an airport into the route only when it has no tickets left, then reverse the route at the end.

jargon.plain: A walk that uses every edge (here, every ticket) exactly once. Hierholzer's algorithm builds one.
Walk until stuck, record the stuck node, step back and continue. The recorded list comes out backwards.
An airport you can fly into but that has no unused ticket out. It can only be the last stop.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a list of [from, to] tickets, e.g. [["JFK","ATL"],["JFK","NRT"],["NRT","LAX"],["LAX","JFK"]]

compare.bruteLabel: Try every ticket order and backtrack
compare.unit: steps (rough; backtracking can be worse than 2^n)

rows.name: Backtracking
rows.note: Take the smallest ticket. If the trip cannot finish, undo it and try the next one.

rows.name: Hierholzer, sorted lists
rows.note: Sorting the destinations costs n log n. After that every ticket is used once, in constant time.

fast.takeaway: Never undo anything. A dead end is simply written down first, and reversing the list puts it last.

stages.title: Sort the tickets
stages.note: Group destinations by airport. Sort each group so the smallest destination sits at the end, ready to pop.

stages.title: Fly the smallest ticket
stages.note: From the airport on top of the walk, take its smallest unused ticket and push the destination.

stages.title: Stuck: record it
stages.note: No ticket left here. Move this airport from the walk to the route, then step back to the one before it.

stages.title: Reverse
stages.note: Airports were recorded last-to-first. Reverse the route to get the real itinerary.

edges.title: Dead end first
edges.why: ATL is smallest from JFK, but flying there ends the trip early. It is recorded first, so after reversing it lands last.

edges.title: Duplicate tickets
edges.why: Each ticket is its own item. Popping removes one copy, so the second copy is still there for the second visit.

edges.title: One ticket
edges.why: JFK is walked, AAA is stuck and recorded, then JFK is stuck and recorded. Reversed: JFK, AAA.

edges.title: Round trip
edges.why: An airport may appear many times in the route. The walk revisits it whenever a ticket leads there.

gotchas.text: Do not append an airport when you first reach it. A greedy walk that records on arrival can get stuck in a dead end with tickets unused. Record on the way back.
Sort so the smallest destination is at the END of each list and pop from the end. Taking from the front (shift, or slicing) is O(n) per ticket.
Array.sort() with no comparator sorts by UTF-16 code units. That is alphabetical for upper-case airport codes, but it would be wrong for numbers, where [10, 9].sort() gives [10, 9].
next[here] = dests[:len(dests)-1] must be written back. dests is a copy of the slice header, so shortening it alone does not remove the ticket from the map.
A missing map key returns a nil slice. len(nil) is 0, so next[here] on an airport with no tickets needs no key check.

recap.key: Walk the smallest ticket until stuck, record the stuck airport, step back, and reverse the recording.
recap.complexity: Time O(n log n). Space O(n).
moves: Sort each airport's destinations, smallest last
Fly the smallest unused ticket from the airport on top
When nothing is left, move it to the route
